title: The sharp approximation ratio for parent-restricted CP-net aggregation
description:
For t complete binary conditional preference tables with t ≥ 3, Algorithm 1 of Ali, Yang and Zilles has exact worst-case ratio 2 − 2/t. Four inputs yield cost 6 versus unrestricted optimum 4, answering the four-thirds question in the AAAI 2024 conclusion.

Each table votes by the OR of all bits except one. Fixing its parent set pairs the all-zero context with the singleton on the omitted attribute. Pooling their votes makes output 0 optimal even though the singleton alone strictly favors output 1. Each re-optimization recovers the corresponding input, and best-input averaging proves the matching upper bound.

The singleton voting pattern comes from the representative-voter example of Endriss and Grandi. The contribution is its realization under overlapping parent sets to attain the ratio after full re-optimization. This result concerns the specific algorithm and binary swap objective. The prior four-thirds guarantee for indegree-at-most-one inputs is compatible.

Internally reviewed, not peer reviewed. The paper gives the general proof. Exact Python replay checks the displayed family through 12 inputs. A partial Lean certificate verifies the four-input costs, its strict violation and one arithmetic inequality.

Under human direction, ChatGPT Astra 6.2 (OpenAI) generated the discovery proof and research packet. OpenAI Codex independently checked the mathematics. GPT-6.2 Sol (OpenAI) checked the literature and prepared the manuscript, replay, partial Lean certificate and illustrations. DannyExperiments is the preferred citation identity. No AI system is proposed as an author.
